target.title: fix(doctor): migrate legacy google provider config to current catalog schema (#102138)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102138. On upgrade, a `models.providers.google` block generated by an
older OpenClaw version passes the persisted **config** schema but fails the
stricter **model-catalog** schema. The whole provider is silently dropped — all
`google/*` models become "not allowed" — and any fallback chain that selects a
gemini model then hangs for 120s on the LLM idle watchdog.

Three schema divergences (confirmed at current `main`):

1. **Missing provider `api`** — catalog validation throws `no "api" specified`
   (`src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:505`).
2. **`input` enum tightened** to `("text"|"image")[]`
   (`src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:165`); legacy blocks store
   `["text","image","audio","video"]`.
3. **`cost.cacheWrite` now required** (`src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:166`);
   legacy `cost` omits it.

The persisted config schema (`src/config/zod-schema.core.ts:382`) still accepts
`audio`/`video` and keeps `cacheWrite` optional, so an old block parses fine
then breaks at catalog load — a schema tightening with no migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair lives in the **Google plugin doctor contract**
(`extensions/google/`), not core. The doctor contract registry already collects
plugin ids from `models.providers` keys
(`src/plugins/doctor-contract-registry.ts:261`) and applies each plugin's
`normalizeCompatibilityConfig`, so a `models.providers.google` block runs the
Google repair without hardcoding google ids or API defaults in the core
migration registry. This follows the established `extensions/ollama` /
`extensions/google-meet` config-compat pattern and keeps provider-owned config
policy in the provider plugin (AGENTS.md:31).

`extensions/google/src/config-compat.ts` (new), for `google`/`google-vertex`
blocks under `openclaw doctor` / `--fix`:

- backfills provider-level `api` (`google` → `google-generative-ai`,
  `google-vertex` → `google-vertex`) — never overwrites a user-set `api`;
- narrows each model's `input` to `["text","image"]`;
- backfills `cost.cacheWrite: 0` when a `cost` object omits it.

Detection and repair share one `providerNeedsApiBackfill` predicate (provider
has no api **and** at least one model has no api → set provider api). A mixed
block — provider no api, one model with api, one without — is therefore fully
repaired and re-detection returns false, fixing the idempotency gap where the
previous asymmetric guard left the api-less model still invalid at catalog
load. Preserves SecretRef `apiKey` / `baseUrl`; leaves non-google providers
untouched.

## Addressing the prior review

- **[P1] Keep Google repair in the plugin doctor contract** — done: moved out
  of `legacy-config-migrations.runtime.models.ts` into the Google plugin
  doctor contract; those core files are now byte-identical to `main`.
- **[P2] Repair mixed model API entries idempotently** — done: shared predicate
  (see above); covered by a dedicated test and the end-to-end proof.

## Evidence

### Focused tests — 10/10 (`extensions/google/src/config-compat.test.ts`)

```
✓ detects a legacy google block
✓ backfills api, narrows input, and fills cost.cacheWrite
✓ preserves the secret-ref apiKey and baseUrl
✓ is idempotent: re-running the migrated config reports no changes
✓ uses the google-vertex api for the google-vertex provider
✓ repairs a mixed model-api block so no model is left without an api (idempotent)
✓ does not overwrite a user-set provider api
✓ leaves models without a cost object untouched
✓ does not touch non-google providers
✓ handles non-record model entries without throwing
```

Core regression (`legacy-config-migrations.runtime.models.test.ts`): 10/10
still pass after removing the core migration.

### End-to-end proof — real plugin doctor-contract path + real ModelRegistry

Part A ran the issue's verbatim legacy block through the real plugin
compatibility entry point (`applyPluginDoctorCompatibilityMigrations` →
`resolvePluginDoctorContracts` → the Google doctor contract), proving the
migration is discovered and applied via the plugin seam:

```
CHANGES (from the google plugin doctor contract):
  - Narrowed models.providers.google.models[0].input to ["text","image"]
  - Set models.providers.google.models[0].cost.cacheWrite to 0
  - Set models.providers.google.api to "google-generative-ai"
```

Part B loaded the block through the real `ModelRegistry` before/after:

```
BEFORE → getError():
   Invalid models.json schema:
     - providers.google.models.0.input.2: must be equal to constant
     - providers.google.models.0.input.3: must be equal to constant
     - providers.google.models.0.cost.cacheWrite: must have required properties cacheWrite
   → find('google','gemini-2.5-pro') === undefined  (silently dropped)
AFTER  → getError(): (none)
   → find('google','gemini-2.5-pro') → gemini-2.5-pro, input ["text","image"]
```

Part C (review P2) repaired a mixed model-api block; the previously api-less
model resolves through the backfilled provider api, `getError()` is clean, and
re-running reports no changes.

### Static checks

- `git diff --check` — clean
- `oxfmt --check` — clean (also enforced by pre-commit)
- `oxlint` — clean

## Scope & honest notes

- Overlaps siblings #102148 / #102154 (same issue, Google plugin doctor
  contract), which earlier review found incomplete (missing `input`
  normalization / compile blockers). This PR does all three fixes with the
  mixed-api idempotency case covered.
- Covers the issue's first problem (migration gap). The second — fast-failing
  an unavailable fallback candidate instead of the 120s watchdog — lands in the
  core model-resolution path and needs a live credentialed google repro; it is
  intentionally tracked on the canonical issue, not in this PR.
- Migrations run under `openclaw doctor` / `--fix`, not automatically at
  startup.
- Scoped to `google` / `google-vertex`; `google-antigravity` /
  `google-gemini-cli` are out of scope (not named in the issue).
